changes.before: Complete collect_readings(values). Visit integer values in order. Ignore negative values, stop at the first zero, and return all positive values seen before that zero. Preserve the input list.
changes.after: Keep positive readings, skip negative ones, and stop at the first zero.

before: continue skips the rest of the current loop iteration. The loop can still visit later items.
break exits the loop completely. Items after it are not visited by that loop.

This example skips a blank label but stops at a special word.
```python
labels = ["Moon", "", "Sun", "STOP", "Stars"]
kept = []
for label in labels:
    if label == "STOP":
        break
    if label == "":
        continue
    kept.append(label)
print(kept)
```
The result is ["Moon", "Sun"]. The blank is skipped; Stars is never reached after STOP.
The instructions after continue are skipped for that item. Moving append before the check would save the item before you tried to skip it.
In your practice, zero is the stop signal and negative numbers are skipped. A positive value is appended normally.
If no zero appears, the loop can visit the whole input. Empty input produces an empty result.
Keep return after the loop so it also runs when break ends the loop early.

before.question: What changes if the zero branch uses continue instead of break for [3, 0, 8]?
choices: The result becomes [3, 8], because the loop continues after zero.
The result stays [3], because both words stop the loop.
The result becomes [0], because zero is appended.
before.explanation: continue skips only the current zero iteration. It allows the later 8 to be processed; break would end the whole loop.
